title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval

transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-07-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Dr. Lena Ortiz (Apex Medical, Head of ML); Marcus Lee (Product); Tariq Hassan (DevOps)

Summary: quick check-in on the quality eval from last week's run, focus on regressed cases, prompt adjustments and guardrail behavior.

[00:00] Jordan: All right, thanks everyone for joining. We'll keep this to about 40 minutes. Quick roll call? 
[00:08] Lena: Hi, Lena here. 
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus. 
[00:11] Tariq: Tariq. 
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Jordan: great. So agenda\u0014review latest quality metrics, look at regression examples, discuss prompt tuning and guardrails, and decide next steps.
[01:05] Priya: I pulled the batch results we ran yesterday \u0014 5k clinical triage prompts, same seed as before. Overall exact-match style accuracy is at 78% versus 82% baseline we saw two weeks ago. So there is a regression concentrated in the 'ambiguous symptoms' bucket.
[01:30] Lena: that's the one we were worried about, yes. Any idea why it dropped? 
[01:35] Priya: early hypothesis is that after we tightened the safety guardrail (phrase-level deny for symptom escalation) the model is being overly conservative and returning 'refer to clinician' more often, which counts as a mismatch in our scoring.
[02:02] Marcus: can you show an example? 
[02:07] Priya: yeah, on slide 3 I pulled three representative cases\u0014
[02:12] [screen share note: Redwood results spreadsheet] 
[02:16] Priya: Case A: patient reports intermittent chest tightness + acid reflux history; reference answer: advise OTC antacid + schedule follow-up; model output: escalate to ER. That's our false positive guardrail firing.
[02:35] Lena: that one worries me \u0014 it's a patient safety area, but we also can't have too many false escalations, it overwhelms triage.
[02:45] Priya: agreed. We checked logs \u0014 the KV cache behavior wasn't the cause; it looks policy/filter trigger score changed after we updated the safety lexicon. The lexicon flagged phrases like 'pressure' and 'tightness' more broadly.
[03:10] Jordan: quick clarification \u0014 when you say 'safety lexicon' that's the guardrail list we shipped in the POC config, correct? 
[03:18] Priya: yes, exactly. We made it more expansive last week per your request to reduce under-escalations.
[03:25] Tariq: From infra side we didn't change model version, correct? It's the same v1.2 open model you recommended. 
[03:30] Priya: correct, model unchanged. It's guardrail + prompt changes.
[03:36] Marcus: what's the scoring metric again? How strict is exact-match? 
[03:40] Priya: scoring uses weighted rubric: primary agreement on disposition (continue home / PCP / urgent / ER) counts most, then specific guidance tokens, then tone. So a change from 'home care' to 'ER' is big penalty.
[04:02] Lena: can we relax the lexicon a bit for certain symptom combos? maybe add exceptions if vitals not mentioned? 
[04:10] Priya: we can. We proposed an ambiguity threshold \u0014 when the model's confidence is low but no vitals/bleeding/shortness noted, fallback to 'recommend PCP' instead of ER. That reduces false positives in tests.
[04:28] Jordan: how would we implement that? runtime flag? prompt-level instruction? 
[04:33] Priya: two levers \u0014 adjust prompt to force consideration of vitals and to bias to lower acuity for ambiguous language, or change guardrail to be conditional, using a post-filter that checks for vitals keywords. For POC I'd recommend prompt tweak first because it's faster to iterate.
[05:00] Marcus: ok, show us the prompt variant. 
[05:03] Priya: reading variant prompt: "You are a clinical triage assistant. If the user mentions vitals (fever, breathing difficulty, bleeding, chest pain with vitals abnormal), escalate. Otherwise, when symptoms are ambiguous, recommend PCP or self-care and include clear next steps." 
[05:30] Lena: sounds reasonable. but I want to see how it affects overall calibration.
[05:36] Priya: we did a quick ablation \u0014 applying prompt variant to a 1k subset increased agreement from 78% to 81% and reduced ER escalations by 35% in ambiguous bucket. However a few borderline urgent cases slipped.
[06:05] Jordan: that's the trade-off. Do you have examples where the prompt made a dangerous miss? 
[06:10] Priya: two cases flagged; in both the patient noted 'sweating and left arm numbness' but without explicit vitals keywords. Prompt bias toward PCP produced 'recommend PCP' where ER desired. We're able to catch these in a secondary pass: if certain symptom n-grams present (like 'arm numbness', 'sweating'), force escalate regardless of vitals tokens.
[06:40] Lena: ok so combine prompt-level bias with symptom exception list. 
[06:45] Priya: yes. We can add exception list + raise confidence threshold for decade.
[06:51] Marcus: what's the plan for regression monitoring? We can't chase every small delta manually. 
[06:55] Priya: suggested: (1) set regression alert threshold at >2.5% drop in primary disposition accuracy on weekly runs; (2) prioritize alerts by impacted bucket size; (3) auto-sample 200 examples for human review when triggered. We're already running the weekly job in the pipeline.
[07:20] Tariq: can you add latency impact? are these extra checks adding notable runtime? 
[07:24] Priya: prompt changes are negligible. Post-filter exception checks add a few ms per request; we measured 12ms median overhead. No capacity changes needed.
[07:40] Jordan: good. next on guardrails \u0014 Marcus mentioned false positives; any plan to surface logs or labels to product team? 
[07:46] Priya: yes the console will show guardrail triggers per request, with hashed PII-safe snippets. We can also expose a 'guardrail heatmap' showing most common trigger rules.
[08:05] Marcus: that will help. Also on evaluation scoring \u0014 current scoring treats 'refer to PCP' vs 'self-care' as different; can we reduce penalty between those? 
[08:15] Priya: we can change rubric weights: make disposition bucket coarser for scoring (three tiers instead of four) to reduce brittle penalties. That raised effective agreement to 83% in our simulation.
[08:35] Lena: ok but we need to keep clinical fidelity. I prefer keeping internal scoring detailed but present a coarse view to product. For decisioning we need the detailed one.
[08:50] Priya: understood; we'll keep detailed scores in infra but add a coarse pass for alerts.
[09:00] Jordan: any security/compliance asks to unblock canary? 
[09:05] Lena: we need SOC 2 summary and encryption details \u0014 how KMS is used in private deployment. Also audit logs for guardrail triggers. 
[09:18] Jordan: we'll send SOC2 and architecture whitepaper. Priya: KMS is supported for private and dedicated; audit logs streaming to customer SIEM is available via S3 sink or syslog.
[09:33] Tariq: great \u0014 for VPC peering, can you confirm one more time the IP ranges and timing? 
[09:38] Priya: yes we'll attach the network runbook. Jordan: ok next \u0014 can we prioritize top 100 failure cases? Lena: yes we'll compile and share by Monday.
[09:52] Marcus: question on canary \u0014 timeline? 
[09:55] Priya: once we run the re-eval and fix prompt/exception lists, we recommend a 2-week canary: 5% traffic routing to dedicated canary with logging and rollback hooks. We can do that in the dedicated environment or private if you prefer.
[10:15] Lena: dedicated is fine for now.
[10:18] Jordan: pricing implications? 
[10:20] Jordan: AE note \u0014 with the canary, there may be small dedicated commit delta; I'll send updated pricing and expected token estimates.
[10:30] Priya: operational ask \u0014 for the re-eval job we need the annotated priority set and your latest reference labels. We'll run the 5k job and share per-bucket diffs.
[10:45] Lena: we'll add notes on edge cases and give the 100 examples as requested.
[10:50] [silence, typing notes]
[11:00] Priya: quick Q \u0014 Marcus, do you want more frequent alerts or the weekly threshold? 
[11:05] Marcus: weekly with immediate high-severity alerts for safety-critical escalations.
[11:10] Jordan: wrap-up \u0014 recap next steps and owners.
[11:15] Jordan: Priya to run re-eval with new prompt + exception list, report back by next Tuesday. Jordan to send SOC2 and pricing by Friday. Apex to provide 100 priority cases by Monday. Tariq to confirm VPC peering window.
[11:40] Lena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:44] Jordan: thanks \u0014 end meeting.

Notes: transcript includes some auto-generated labels; occasional ASR errors: 'triage' was sometimes transcribed as 'try age'.
